detail.doc: num 0 to 0.95: share of any per-card limit at which the worker is told to wrap up (commit, record findings, publish a draft pull request); a value under 0.5 is raised to 0.5 (0 keeps the agent's own, 0.85 for the built-ins)
int 0 to 10: failed attempts at one stage before Belai blocks the card (0 keeps the agent's own). Not `autonomy.max_attempts`, which retries a workflow step
int 0 to 50: times a card may go back to be resumed after its budget ran out with progress made, before it is blocked for a person (0 keeps the agent's own, 5 by default)
num 0 to 10000: estimated cost in US dollars at which a worker's claim on one card ends (0 keeps each agent's own; the built-in agents allow $8 to $25)
int 0 to 400: tool rounds per pass (0 keeps the agent's own)
int 0 to 1000: goal passes per card, a safety rail beside the cost limit (0 keeps the agent's own)
int 0 to 10080: minutes per card, a safety rail (0 keeps the agent's own)
list of path globs (feGlobMatch dialect) that stop an approval, besides the built-in list
bool: log every model call with its input hash
int 1 to 1440: minutes a started crew or worker dispatch may go without a session before the attempt fails `card_unclaimed` and retries
enum `observe`, `suggest`, `draft_pr`, `auto_merge_low_risk` ("approve when ready"): autonomy of a repository of a managed organisation that has no settings row (13.2)
int 1 to 168: hours a crew step may wait for a machine before the run ends `no_host_timeout`
int 1 to 1000: runs of the tenant that may wait for a machine at once; they do not count against `autonomy.concurrency`
bool: transcripts show A2A rows (broadcasts, messages, replies, acks) by default; a viewer can override it locally
bool: whether the workers and crews a workflow or schedule starts stop at permission asks (sent as the dispatch's `ask`; docs/factory-engine.md, "Stay and replicas")
enum `on`, `strict`, `off` (`off` is refused for worker crews)
enum `goal`, `agent`, `plan`, `auto` (default mode for crews the factory starts)
str: an email domain such as `acme.example`, or empty
bool: the hand-worked comparison, which adds the refinement and hand-off overhead
bool: price the decisions System One scored
bool: master switch. Off, every `/delivery` read answers `{"enabled":false}` and nothing is computed
num 1 to 400: productive hours per person-month
int 1 to 120: minutes without an action that end a sitting
num 0 to 365: days a team takes per card
num 0 to 365: days a team takes per pull request
num 0 to 720: hours a team waits to decide, compared with the measured time
num 0 to 365: days a team takes per issue
num 0.5 to 10: multiplier for agent work no role covers
pct: refinement and hand-off overhead as a share of build and decision hours
num 0 to 10000: USD per hour for the overhead
bool: the People and Contributors pages
num 0 to 10000: USD per hour for the hours people spent in the factory (the cost side)
num 0 to 10000: USD per hour for agent work no role covers
num 0 to 60: minutes of reading per 100 changed lines of a review
bool: price agent work by role
int 1 to 50: runs one delivery or sighting may start; triggers past it, by priority, are skipped as `fanout_cap`
bool: publish gate results as check runs (needs `checks: write`)
bool: send `If-None-Match` on every live read
bool: never push to protected branches
int 0 to 5000: most calls an installation makes in a clock hour for default workflows (13.4)

string `auto`, `pix_sandbox`, `self_hosted`, `host:<uuid>` or `label:<name>`, the crew node's `runOn` grammar (`factoryRunOnValid`): where a crew node, a default or a scan that names no `runOn` runs, and the preference that orders the hosts a node's own `runOn` admits (12.5)
enum `none`, `auto`: the fallback that goes with `hosts.runOn`; a node that writes its own `runOnFallback` keeps it
int, calls per day, shared with the sandbox
enum `safest`, `stable`, `latest`, `rolling`, `pinned` (the first four are the Safe Harbour picks, see `pix-sandbox-safe-harbour.md`)
`"all_active"` or list of installation logins; same write as `PUT /orgs/{id}`
enum `6h`, `1h`, `webhook_only`: cadence of the existing installation metadata sweep
enum `minimum` (sca, malscan, secrets), `all`, `custom`; `custom` needs `security.scanners.custom` (list of scanner ids)
bool: add a new key's public key to the person's GitHub account
enum `primary`, `noreply`, `ask`: the address on the commit
enum `readd`, `ask`: what to do when GitHub no longer lists a key
enum `30`, `7`, `0` (right away), `-1` (leave it on GitHub): how long a replaced key stays on GitHub
str, read-only, identity the threshold was set for
bool: a person may override any decision

Answer the question a session is waiting on: a permission (allow_once or deny) or a clarifying question (answer text).
Decisions the factory made: how many, how many went to a person and how fast people answered, how many a rule handled.
Who took part in the factory's work: people, their actions and time, and contributors on record.

What the factory's delivery is worth. focus benefit: what it delivered and what a team would have needed (default today). fte_hours: the hours, and people for a month, a team would need. by_hand_cost: what the same work would cost with agile teams by hand (default this month). return: the return on model use. By-hand figures are estimates from Settings.
What model use cost: spend and tokens today or over a range, the budget pace, and cost by model on screen. Use for "what was my spend".
Software Factory headline numbers: agents working, cards done, draft PRs, gates holding, tokens and spend, what needs the caller.
Match a repository the caller said out loud to one they can use, and the hosts that can take it. Pass their words as spoken.
Delete a note, when the caller asks you to forget it. Find its id with recall first and say which note it is.
Where sessions hit trouble: tool errors, failed or interrupted turns and denied permissions, by tool, model and host, and hosts on an older belai.
Turn hold music on while waiting on a session, or off.
The workload on the caller's hosts: online hosts, sessions against slots, full and offline hosts, budget used per host, and how often hosts went offline.
Whether the factory's figures can be trusted: for each lifecycle stage, whether its record matches the source, has a gap, or is not captured yet.
The caller's Pix Sandboxes and self-managed hosts, whether they are online, and which repositories they offer.
Software Factory workflow runs, newest first.
Coding-agent sessions, newest first, with optional filters.
What is waiting on the caller: approvals, agent questions, offline hosts.
The oldest open checkpoints (things waiting on a person or an outside party), oldest first, with how long each has waited and the count by kind.
The trend of outcomes: what the factory delivered and abandoned in a window against the same length before, and decisions made and escalated.
Prepare to turn permission asks off on a running session, so it stops waiting for approvals, and get the read-back. Only when the caller asks for it.

Prepare to start a coding-agent session and get the read-back to say. For several sessions, call it once per session in the same reply: they join one read-back (up to 5). Nothing starts until start_session after the caller says yes.
Prepare to stop a running session and get the read-back.

Whether a queue is growing: open now, the server's trend against the start of the window, work in against work done, typical wait and the oldest item. stage "queue" is every checkpoint plus queued runs and sessions.
Search the notes kept from earlier calls.

Keep a note for future calls: a preference, a standing instruction or a fact the caller wants kept ("always use plan mode on vdb-site"). Only when they ask you to remember, or state a lasting preference.
Everything recent on one repository: session totals, factory runs, open findings, SLSA level.
One factory run: its steps and their status, and its PR.
Send a message to a running session's agent, after reading it back to the caller.
One session in detail: state, repository, branch and PR, what it last said, and any question it is waiting on.

Totals across recent sessions: how many, live, failed, stopped, tokens, typical length. Optionally for one repository and grouped. Use this for any "how many sessions" question; never add numbers up yourself.
Start every session in the read-back. Only after the caller said yes to it, in their very last reply.
Stop the session after the caller said yes to the stop read-back.
Turn permission asks off on the session, after the caller said yes to the asks-off read-back.
Turn permission asks back on for a running session, when the caller asks. No read-back needed.
